hardinessNote: Hardy in most of the UK, approximately −15 to −10°C (RHS 369164).
visual: Large rosy-purple leaves netted with charcoal-grey veins, silvered between · dense mound, colour spring to autumn · small flowers on wiry stems in summer
soilWarning: Crowns lift; replant deeper every few years
water: Water in dry spells, especially in pots; avoid sitting wet in winter.
prune: Remove tatty leaves in spring; cut off spent flower stems after flowering.
cvs: 'Palace Purple' – bronze-purple leaves · FOREVER PURPLE ('Tnheufp') – glossy purple, compact · 'Paris' – silvered green, rose flowers
resilience: Tough, long-lived foliage plant; dislikes waterlogged soil, especially in winter. Pests: vine weevil grubs, occasionally slugs.
uses: Borders · containers · woodland edges · ground cover
foliage: evergreen to semi-evergreen; large rounded rosy-purple leaves with dark charcoal veins
uncertain: name: Oscar's label read 'Heuchera hybrida 'Wild Any''; Oscar confirmed 2026-10-24 it is 'Wild Rose'. RHS 369164: Heuchera 'Wild Rose' (Primo Series), bred by Hans Hansen at Walters Gardens (US PP29923).
size: Walters Gardens and Proven Winners give 8–10 in tall × 18–20 in wide (20–25 cm × 45–50 cm); Ashridge to 40 × 40 cm. Not RHS.
foliage: RHS lists evergreen / semi-evergreen; rosy-purple leaves with charcoal veining (RHS, Proven Winners, Ashridge).
peak: Mar-Nov is the foliage season it is sold on; flowering months not confirmed.
compliance: the RHS research for this batch listed 'Wild Rose' PBR; grant number not found.
toxicity: the ASPCA lists Heuchera as non-toxic to dogs, cats and horses.
ratings, aspect, water and prune: from the Forge genus-level draft, not sourced for the cultivar.
sources: RHS 369164 (search snippets): H5, evergreen/semi-evergreen, rosy-purple leaves with charcoal veins
